title: Partner history reduced high-water probability error by 2.32% on six Atlantic links in 2018-2024
abstract: We tested whether nearby gauge history improves probabilities of high next-day water levels beyond a local model with NOAA tide calculations. We used four Atlantic gauges, six directed links, fixed calendar-month 95th-percentile thresholds from 2015-2017, and chronological fits for 2018-2024. Empirical training-error distributions gave a mean Brier score reduction of 2.32%. The conditional 95% two-year block interval was 1.09% to 3.25%. Five link estimates were positive; Boston history made the score worse at The Battery. Older partner history at lags 8 and 9 gave an uncertain mean gain of 0.08%. The test event rate was 9.22%, so the initial percentile does not describe test rarity. Seven test years, selected complete records, fitted-error assumptions, uncertain thresholds, and tide calculations fetched in 2026 limit inference. The result does not establish an operational flood warning gain or a physical cause. The package gives source hashes, exact daily evidence, all forecasts, scores, resamples, figures, an independent arithmetic audit, a source audit, and an offline repeat.

display.caption: High-water probability score gains on six Atlantic links and planned checks. The event threshold uses the fixed initial period. Right-panel intervals use two-year blocks and fixed fitted forecasts. These are statistical events, not official flood levels.
